## The C++ options objects and modules (`ADD_ARG`) {#sec-ch11-options}

### Summary

Every configurable part of kintera is a pair: an options struct that holds plain values, and a module that is
built from the options and holds tensors. The options struct is what the YAML reader fills and what a C++ or
Python caller may edit before building the module. Each option field is declared with one macro, `ADD_ARG`, which
gives a chained setter and a getter of the same name.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One options struct per module, with fluent setters and getters.

**Data.** Plain C++ values and vectors; modules hold `torch` buffers built from them.

**Placement.** Options are filled by `from_yaml` or by hand, then passed to the module constructor.

**Activation.** Always; each field has an in-class default.

**Guarantee / limits.** Editing options after the module is built does not rebuild the module (hypothesis).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

The options of a module are reached in C++ as `module->options`, and in Python as the read-only attribute
`options` (@sec-ch11-python-api).

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme is an interface.

### Numerical method

No numerical method and no figure: this scheme is an interface.

: Code map of the options objects. {#tbl-ch11-options-code}

`ADD_ARG(T, name)` ({{< code src/add_arg.h >}}) expands to a private member `name_` and four public functions:
`name(const T&)` and `name(T&&)` set the member and return `*this`, so calls chain; `name() const` and `name()`
return a reference to it. Under the CUDA compiler the getters are marked host and device. A default is given by
writing `= value` after the macro.

The kinetics options `KineticsOptionsImpl` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsOptionsImpl >}}) derive
from the species thermodynamics struct and declare: `Tref` (default $298.15\,\mathrm{K}$), `Pref` (default
$101325\,\mathrm{Pa}$), one sub-option per rate form (`arrhenius`, `coagulation`, `evaporation`, `three_body`,
`lindemann_falloff`, `troe_falloff`, `sri_falloff`, `kb_falloff`, each default-constructed), and the flags
`evolve_temperature`, `verbose` and `offset_zero` (all default `false`).

The thermodynamics options `ThermoOptionsImpl` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoOptionsImpl >}}) derive from
the same species struct and declare: `Tref` (default $300\,\mathrm{K}$), `Pref` (default $10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$),
`max_iter` (default 10), `ftol` (default $10^{-6}$), `gas_floor` (default $10^{-20}$), `verbose` and
`offset_zero` (default `false`), the sub-option `nucleation`, and `uv_solver` (default `auto`). The defaults of
`Tref` and `Pref` differ from those of `KineticsOptionsImpl`, so a file without `reference-state/Tref` gives the
two option sets different reference temperatures. Whether any result depends on that difference is not tested
(hypothesis). The flags `use_nasa9_cp` (default `false`), `use_h2_cp` (default `false`) and `h2_cp_mode`
(default `equilibrium`) belong to the shared species struct `SpeciesThermoImpl`
({{< code src/species.hpp SpeciesThermoImpl >}}). `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}) sets them from
`reference-state`. It reads `h2-cp-mode` only when `use-h2-cp` is present, and accepts only `equilibrium` or
`normal` there.

The same reader registers species differently from the kinetics reader: the first species of the file is always
a vapor; the vapors and clouds are taken from the `nucleation`, `coagulation` and `evaporation` entries; and every
species with `phase: gas` is added as a vapor, every other declared phase as a cloud. A contradiction between the
reactions and a declared phase is refused. For each nucleation reaction whose latent heat at `Tref` (the
stoichiometric sum of `u0_R`) is not positive, it issues a warning.

The extrapolation calls of `ThermoX` take a separate plain struct, `ExtrapOptions`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ExtrapOptions >}}), with `dlnp`, `dz`, `grav`, `ds_dlnp`, `ds_dz`, `verbose` and
`rainout` (all zero or `false` by default); it is
not read from YAML.

The kinetics module `KineticsImpl` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsImpl >}}) exposes three calls:

1. `forward(temp, pres, conc, extra)` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsImpl::forward >}}) takes
   temperature [K] of shape `(...)`, pressure [Pa] of shape `(...)` and concentration
   [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] of shape `(..., nspecies)`. It returns the reaction rates
   [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] of shape `(..., nreaction)`, the derivative of the rate constants with
   respect to concentration of shape `(..., nspecies, nreaction)`, and an optional derivative with respect to
   temperature.
2. `forward_with_rate_constants` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}})
   returns the same three plus the raw forward rate constants, for a Jacobian that does not depend on state kept
   in the module.
3. `jacobian(temp, conc, cvol, rate, rc_ddC, rc_ddT, rate_constants)`
   ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}) returns the reaction-space Jacobian of shape
   `(..., nreaction_aug, nspecies)`; its header comment says `rate_constants` is required at zero solid
   abundance.

The free function `evolve_implicit(rate, stoich, jacobian, dt)`
({{< code src/kinetics/evolve_implicit.hpp evolve_implicit >}}) returns the concentration change of shape
`(..., nspecies)` from one backward-Euler step; the system it solves is @sec-ch10's subject.

: Tests of the options objects. {#tbl-ch11-options-tests}

The options objects are exercised by every test that builds a module; this draft has not mapped which test
covers which field.

### Limits

- Editing an options field after its module is built is not reflected in the module's buffers until the module is
  reset. This is a hypothesis from reading `ArrheniusImpl::reset`
  ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::reset >}}), which copies options into buffers; not tested.
- The thermodynamics modules `ThermoX` and `ThermoY` are described here only through their options; their calls
  are listed in @sec-ch11-python-api.
